newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Strathmore bids for its shares at 34 cts.
newsitem.headline: Strathmore bids for its shares at 34 cts.

text.p: Strathmore Group Ltd told shareholders on Thursday it intended to offer 34 cents per share and a maximum price of 36 cents in its bid to buy back 15 million shares, a quarter of the company's capital.
Strathmore shares last traded on the market on Tuesday at 34 cents.
It said it had been unable to find suitable investments and instead would buy back the shares.
On a cash basis, Strathmore said it had made a profit of about $575,000 in the first quarter.
Using adopted accounting policies the result would be somewhat lower due to the amortisation of goodwill relating to investments and due to equity accounting of trading losses.

It said progress at CES Communications had been slower than hoped due to unexpected delays in the final technical designs of the encryption phones being developed. However final commercial products were now being produced by the licences and CES is expected to move into profit in the near future.
Strathmore has divested all holdings of listed shares and its stake in New Zealand Oil and Gas had been sold at a profit of about $250,000. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
